title: Changelog generator: improve customer_safe_summary templating (limit jargon + always include compatibility)
author: Michael Nguyen
description: Context: We’ve had multiple instances of published model changelog entries where the top-line summary used internal-ish jargon (e.g. “routing policy”, “kernel swap”, “KV cache tuning”) and, more importantly, where the summary omitted compatibility caveats that were present elsewhere in the entry. This created confusion during rollouts (Support escalations and SUP-18502 specifically cited “what does this mean for our pinned version + tool calling?”). This PR tightens the generator’s customer_safe_summary rendering rules: (1) enforce a jargon budget (simple term substitutions + removal of internal platform terms) and a hard length cap, (2) guarantee a Compatibility sentence is always present (even when the underlying event payload doesn’t include a user-authored compatibility note), and (3) add test fixtures + lint checks so summaries can’t regress. Changes: Update templating to render customer_safe_summary from a structured set of candidate sentences (ChangeType sentence + Compatibility sentence + optional Deprecation sentence), dedupe/normalize whitespace, and ensure deterministic ordering. Add a small allowlist/denylist word pass with safe replacements (e.g., “routing policy” -> “request routing settings”, “kernel” -> “runtime optimization”, “KV cache” -> removed unless explicitly customer-relevant). Add fallback compatibility content: when compatibility fields are missing, we emit a conservative statement that links to the compatibility matrix / model page and explicitly calls out that pinned versions are unchanged unless the entry indicates otherwise. Add validations: if entry has tool/function calling, response_format/structured output, or context window changes, compatibility sentence must mention it. Add unit tests for: missing compatibility note, deprecation-only event, perf-only event, multiple updates in one day, and redaction of internal terms. Add snapshot tests for customer_safe_summary output across a set of real-ish fixtures. Rollout/ops: No schema changes. Generator output changes only. Expect a small number of existing drafts in staging to change wording; published entries are not rewritten by this PR. Next: follow-up PR in redwood-docs to align docs-side style linting with the same denylist to avoid drift.
commits: changelog/templates: refactor customer_safe_summary to sentence-based renderer
changelog/templates: add compatibility sentence fallback + rules for tool calling/structured output
changelog/lint: add jargon denylist + safe replacements
tests: add fixtures + snapshot tests for customer_safe_summary
ops: add debug log line with summary truncation reason (staging only)
review_conversation: Elliot Price: The denylist replacements look good, but please avoid “runtime optimization” if we can—still feels a bit inside baseball. Can we use “performance improvements” instead unless the entry explicitly talks about runtime compatibility?

Michael Nguyen (author): Good call. Updated replacements: “kernel/runtime optimization” -> “performance improvements” by default, and only mention “runtime” when compatibility fields specify minimum runtime version. Added tests for both paths.

Marissa Cole: Requirement from PM-801: compatibility note must always be present and must be actionable. The fallback sentence should include where to look + what to do if you’re pinned. Can we explicitly mention pinned model_version + changelog URL in the console, not here? (But at least say “If you pin versions, no action is required unless…”).

Michael Nguyen (author): Updated fallback to: “Compatibility: No action required for pinned versions unless noted above. See the model page for supported features (tool calling, structured output, context).” Added link token so docs/console can render as a proper link.

Dev Patel: This addresses the Support complaint. Two asks: (1) ensure we don’t say “no action required” when there is a deprecation in the same entry; (2) add a test for confusing jargon from SUP-18502 (“routing policy”).

Michael Nguyen (author): Done. Deprecation sentence now overrides the “no action required” fragment, and I added a fixture that includes “routing policy” in internal notes to make sure it never appears in customer_safe_summary.
Jada Williams: Any impact to approval workflow? We shouldn’t be changing the state machine here, but do we need to surface “summary truncated” as a reviewer hint in the draft UI?

Michael Nguyen (author): No workflow changes. I added a staging-only debug log + metric counter for truncation. I agree draft UI hint would be useful but kept that out of scope; I added a TODO and a note in README for a follow-up.
Elliot Price: Approving with the wording update. Please keep the denylist small and prefer substitutions over deletions when possible.
Marissa Cole: Approved. This matches the PRD expectations for customer-safe summaries.
Dev Patel: Approved from Support readiness.
release_notes: Customer-facing changelog summaries now always include a Compatibility sentence and avoid internal jargon.
Generator enforces length caps and deterministic ordering for customer_safe_summary.
